paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus sends out His people, and the work is His, not theirs. He tells them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few," and the first thing He asks of them is to pray: "Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest." (Luke 10:2) He sends them with no purse, no bag and no sandals, so they have to lean on Him. And when a town says no, the message doesn't change: "The kingdom of God is near." (Luke 10:11)

Now look at what happens when the seventy-two come back thrilled that "even the demons submit to us in Your name." (Luke 10:17) Jesus is glad with them, and He does give them authority. Then He says, "Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven." (Luke 10:20) Friend, that's the part to hold onto: our biggest joy isn't what we get to DO for Him, it's that we belong to Him.

And that belonging is a gift, not a prize for the smartest in the room. Jesus praises the Father for revealing these things "to little children," and says the Son reveals the Father to those He chooses. (Luke 10:21-22) Then He tells the disciples, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see." (Luke 10:23) So, baker, when you open the Word, you're not just reading old pages. You're seeing what many prophets and kings longed to see, and that is worth getting excited about!
